== Biography ==
William was born about 1781. He was the son of [[Glasgow-1549|John Glasgow]].  He passed away about 1853.
== Research Notes ==
=== Possible Philadelphia death, 1855 ===

A Findmypast transcript of the Philadelphia Board of Health Registers of Deaths records William Glasgow, aged 70, with death dated 25 March 1855. It describes the register as Burial, but supplies no separate burial day. Its indexed birth year of 1785 is calculated from the age, not an exact birthday. The parish and diocese are Philadelphia; the address field is blank.<ref>Findmypast, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=US%2FBMD%2FPENN-BUR%2F01460438 Historical Society of Pennsylvania, Deaths & Burials, William Glasgow, US/BMD/PENN-BUR/01460438, Board of Health Registers of Deaths, 1853–1855]; provider derivative transcript inspected 4 November 2026; original record or gravestone image uninspected.</ref>

This is a possible comparison for William’s Pennsylvania identity, not an assigned death record. His earlier account gives birth about 1781 and death about 1853; the more specific inherited death date is 7 February 1853. Those estimated dates have not been established by the 1825 will. Their differences from this transcript need investigation and do not by themselves exclude a match. The transcript names no relative, birthplace or occupation connecting the Philadelphia man to William, and no death date is changed. The original death entry may supply distinguishing details.

=== Original Huntingdon will reviewed — 24 October 2026 ===

The original 1825 will explicitly names William among John’s children and gives him a $200 legacy. The existing William account is the compatible circa-1781 son already represented in this family. This is direct evidence for the family relationship, while the at-sea birth and exact later adult dates remain inherited claims rather than facts established by the will. The original will names wife Margaret, sons Richard, William, John, Samuel, Matthew, James and Taylor, and daughters Hannah and Jane. James and Taylor receive the 322-acre, 72-perch home tract jointly, subject to Margaret’s support and the legacies, and are appointed executors. The register records probate and the grant to both executors on 12 March 1825. The will names no mother for the children, no Hunter maiden surname, and no Scottish father for its testator. The widow Margaret is not automatically each child’s mother. The exact percentage assesses the complete father–child identification and is subjective. The original establishes the named family roles; identification of later adults, precise vital dates, maternal parentage and earlier Scottish ancestry require their own evidence. No live WikiTree save or vital-field change is made.<ref>[https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99B-T8NH?cc=1999196&wc=9PM6-7MN%3A268496101%2C268530601 Huntingdon County, Pennsylvania, Wills 1822–1847, volumes 3–4, register pp. 139–140; John Glasgow of Antis Township, will 21 January 1825, proved 12 March 1825; FamilySearch, Pennsylvania Probate Records, image 103 of 607. Original full page and both page details inspected 24 October 2026.]</ref>

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1549]] is assessed at 65% (probable). William’s c 1781 birth is compatible with John’s c 1758 generation and the inherited family sequence. The same John also has the later Taylor Wilson child, which is chronologically possible.

Probable from the family account, without a held parent-naming record for William. The selected John’s own ancestry is a separate question.

Next useful test: Check John’s estate or William’s original death entry for the parent name.
